response.reason: The cited clause (Art. 26(2)(a) of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011) establishes that the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance is mandatory if omitting it could mislead consumers, especially if the labeling would otherwise suggest a different origin. The verdict turns on this requirement, stating that both the product and its primary ingredient are declared as 'Deutschland', so there is no risk of misleading the consumer. The clause is directly relevant and supports the legal grounding of the verdict.
